chapter: Childhood in Oklahoma, Kansas City and Tulsa
title: Earl Bostic and how he came to play trumpet
summary: Earl Bostic got a clarinet from the church; Simmons wanted a saxophone but only trumpets were left.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: So, how I started playing trumpet. Earl Bostic was a very gifted young man. He would appear on Saturday night, amateur shows, you know, and he'd play the part of Harold Teen. He had the big leg pants and he'd whistle and play ukelele. win first prize And he'd always (unintelligible). So, he was a Catholic, but he was going to public school, because our Catholic school didn't go any further than about sixth grade. But they had instruments.

So the church gave Earl a clarinet so that he could play in the public school band. And Earl picked it up in no time, and he got a scholarship to Xavier University in New Orleans. And when he graduated, he graduated and stayed on as bandmaster for about two years, and he left there and he went New York.

When he got the clarinet, I wanted to be a saxophone player. So I went over and asked them for a saxophone. I was a Catholic, too, at that time. They didn't have any saxophones. All they had left was trumpets. I said, "Well, give me that."
So that's how I played trumpet. All through school, I started on the fourth part and when I finished school, I was a soloist. I passed from the first trumpet to the soloist spot.
